deep.reconstruction:
The page has two independent parts. The upper ~2/3 is a sheet of identities among theta constants. The lower third is elementary algebra that belongs to the 'Aufgabe' on the next page (unknowns α,β,γ,δ with αa+βb+γc+δd=0 and a/α+b/β+c/γ+d/δ=0).

PART A: theta identities, genus-3 labelling by 8 symbols.

(a) Notation. The symbols are a,b,c,d,e1,e2,e3,e4, and later a,a',b,b',c,c',d,d'. A theta characteristic is named by a subset of this 8-set, taken modulo complement. This is the standard genus-3 scheme (2^6 = 64 = 2^7/2 classes):
- the empty set ϑ(0) and the 35 four-sets give the 36 even characteristics;
- the 28 two-sets give the 28 odd characteristics.

Written mod 2 as symmetric differences, the sum of characteristics is the symmetric difference of the sets.

(b) Reading of the left sides. Each left side has the form ϑ[m]·Σ± ϑn1 ϑn2 ϑn3, with n1,n2,n3 two-sets (odd). The only sensible reading is that Σ± ϑn1ϑn2ϑn3 is the Jacobian determinant det(∂ϑ[n_i]/∂v_j)(0), i = 1..3, of three odd theta functions at v=0. This reading is mine, but it is supported by weights: one even constant (weight 1/2) times a genus-3 Jacobian (weight 3/2+1 = 5/2) has weight 3. Each right side is a sum of products of six even theta constants, also weight 3.

The page therefore records genus-3 'Jacobi derivative formulas' of the type ϑ[m]·D(n1,n2,n3) = P1 ± P2, with P1, P2 monomials of degree six in theta-nulls. Examples:
- Line 1: ϑ(ace3e4)·D(ab,ac,bd) = ϑabce3 ϑabce4 ϑabde1 ϑabde2 ϑabcd ϑade3e4 + ϑbcde4 ϑbcde3 ϑacde2 ϑacde1 ϑbce3e4 ϑ(0).
- Lines 2 and 3: the same type for the triples (cd,ac,bd) and (ac,ab,cd). The prefactor is not written there, but see (c).
- Line 6: ϑ(0)·D(ab,e3e4,e1e2) = ϑabce3 ϑabce4 ϑabde1 ϑabde2 ϑbde3e4 ϑade3e4 + ϑabde3 ϑabde4 ϑabce1 ϑabce2 ϑbce3e4 ϑace3e4.
- Line 7, in the relabelled alphabet: ϑ(0)·D(aa',bb',cc') = a single product of six constants.

Below these come attempts with 'Σe', 'e_ν', square roots √(ϑ…ϑ…), and primed e's (e1', e2'). They look like an effort to write general/symmetrised versions, e.g. ϑab·Σ_e Σ± ϑ(ab')ϑab ϑ(a'b') = …. They are heavily corrected and incomplete, and I cannot reconstruct them reliably.

(c) My consistency check (characteristic bookkeeping). In a valid theta-constant identity, every monomial must have the same total characteristic mod 2 (and mod complement).
- Line 1: left ace3e4 + ab + ac + bd = {a,d,e3,e4}. Both right monomials sum to {b,c,e1,e2}, the complement. Consistent.
- Line 2: both monomials give {a,d,e1,e2}. The left triple gives {a,b}, which forces the missing prefactor to be {a,c,e3,e4} (or its complement).
- Line 3: both monomials give {e1,e2}. The triple gives {b,d}, which again forces prefactor ϑ(ace3e4). So lines 1–3 are a family under the common factor ϑ(ace3e4).
- Line 6: both monomials give {a,b,e1..e4} ≡ {c,d}, which equals the left side ∅ + ab + e1e2 + e3e4. Consistent.

PART B: algebra for the next page's problem.

(i) Determinant. The rows are (1, ββ1, 1/ββ1'), (1, γγ1, 1/γγ1'), (1, δδ1, 1/δδ1'). Riemann expands the 3×3 determinant along the third column:
y_β(x_γ−x_δ) + y_γ(x_δ−x_β) + y_δ(x_β−x_γ).
Using Σ(x-differences) = 0 he rewrites it as (x_γ−x_δ)(y_β−y_δ) + …, i.e. (γγ1−δδ1)(1/ββ1 − 1/δδ1) + ….

(ii) Linear transfer rules. He writes rules of the type
λ''(α''−β'') = λ(α−β) + λ'(α'−β'),
λ''(1/α''−1/β'') = λ(1/α−1/β) + λ'(1/α'−1/β').
The first two lines are analogous, with a 'pole' ρ: −λλ'(α''−1/ρ) = (α−1/ρ)λ + (α'−1/ρ')λ'. Multiplying such a pair gives quadratic quantities (α−β)(1/α−1/β) = −(α−β)²/(αβ). These are exactly the quantities (βab'−αa'b)(ab'/β−a'b/α) used on the next page.

(iii) Factorisation. Put f(α,α') = λ(α+1/α) + λ'(α'+1/α') + λλ'(α/α'+α'/α). The last line is
f(α,α') − f(β,β') = λ(α−β)(1−1/(αβ)) + λ'(α'−β')(1−1/(α'β')) + λλ'(α/α'−β/β')(1−α'β'/(αβ)).
This is a correct factorisation of each difference. The line before it, λα+λ'α'+λλ'(λ/α+λ'/α'+1), is probably misread or abandoned.
errors: Line 5 as transcribed (ϑbce3e4·Σ±ϑabϑacϑbd = ϑabce3ϑbcde2ϑacde3ϑabde2ϑade1e3ϑade3e4 + ϑabde3ϑacde2ϑbcde3ϑabce2ϑbce1e3ϑbce3e4) fails the parity bookkeeping. Its two monomials give different totals ({e2,e3} vs {a,d,e1,e4}), and neither equals the left side {b,d,e3,e4}. Either some subscripts are misread or Riemann's line is a slip/abandoned draft; I cannot decide from the image.
Line 7 as transcribed (factor ϑbb'dd') fails parity. Replacing ϑbb'dd' by ϑbb'c'd makes the total {a,a',b,b',c,c'} ≡ {d,d'}, matching the left side. This is probably a reading error, not Riemann's.

Line 7 is a one-term formula, whereas the analogous line 6 (three disjoint pairs ab, e1e2, e3e4) has two terms. Either line 7 is incomplete or the two triples play different roles; this cannot be settled from the page.
The lower 'Σe', 'e_ν', √ϑ formulas are fragmentary, with cancellations and unclosed brackets. No complete statement can be checked.
In Part B, line 3 is transcribed with λ' on the left. By analogy with line 4 it should be λ''. The first line has 1/ρ where 1/ρ'' would be expected; this is unclear from the image.

results.what: Genus-3 Jacobian (derivative) formulas: one even theta constant times the Jacobian determinant of three odd theta functions at 0 equals a sum of two products of six even theta constants. Characteristics are labelled by 2- and 4-subsets of 8 symbols; the parity bookkeeping is consistent for lines 1,2,3,6.
results.modern_name: Generalized Jacobi derivative formula in genus 3 (Jacobian nullwerte of odd theta functions)
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius (1885, 'Über die constanten Factoren der Thetareihen'), Weber (1876, genus-3 Abelian functions), Thomae; modern treatment Igusa (1980), Fay

results.what: Use of the 8-symbol labelling of the 64 genus-3 characteristics (∅ and 4-sets even, 2-sets odd)
results.modern_name: Aronhold/Weber labelling of genus-3 theta characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (p=3 lectures, 1860s), Weber 1876, Cayley/Aronhold for bitangents

results.what: Cofactor expansion of the determinant |1, x_i, y_i| and its rewriting as products of differences
Factorisation f(α,α')−f(β,β') for f = λ(α+1/α)+λ'(α'+1/α')+λλ'(α/α'+α'/α), and the quadratic invariant (α−β)(1/α−1/β), used for the system αa+βb+γc+δd=0, a/α+…=0

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's work on p=3 and his set-labelling of characteristics are known, from the Werke and Weber's 1876 book. A page of explicit genus-3 Jacobian-of-odd-thetas formulas, written as sums of two degree-6 monomials, is a notable unpublished detail. It anticipates the formulas usually attributed to Frobenius/Thomae/Weber, but it is a fragmentary scratch sheet with unproven identities, and the Göttingen circle plausibly knew such relations. The rating is moderate, not high.
